questions.question:
The `np-baseline` namespace runs a web server Pod named `web` (label `app=web`, serving HTTP on port `80`) and a client Pod named `client`. No NetworkPolicy exists in the namespace yet, so every Pod can reach every other Pod.

Create a NetworkPolicy named `default-deny-ingress` in the `np-baseline` namespace that denies all incoming traffic to every Pod in the namespace.

The policy must apply to every Pod, must restrict `Ingress` only, and must not permit any traffic at all.

Do not delete or modify any existing Pod.

verification.description: NetworkPolicy default-deny-ingress exists
The policy selects every Pod and permits nothing
Pod client can no longer reach web

questions.question:
The `np-tiers` namespace already carries a NetworkPolicy named `default-deny` that denies all ingress to every Pod. It contains three Pods: `api` (label `app=api`, serving HTTP on port `80`), `frontend` (label `role=frontend`) and `scanner` (label `role=scanner`).

Create a NetworkPolicy named `api-allow-frontend` in the `np-tiers` namespace that allows Pods labelled `role=frontend` to reach the Pods labelled `app=api` on TCP port `80`.

When you are finished `frontend` must be able to reach `api` on port `80`, and `scanner` must not.

Do not modify or delete the `default-deny` policy, and do not change any Pod label.

verification.description: api-allow-frontend applies Ingress rules to the app=api Pods
Pod frontend can reach api on port 80
Pod scanner is denied access to api

questions.question:
The `np-crossns` namespace runs the Pod `payments` (label `app=payments`, serving HTTP on port `80`) and already carries a NetworkPolicy named `default-deny` that denies all ingress.

Two other namespaces each contain a Pod named `probe`: `np-crossns-monitor`, which is labelled `purpose=monitoring`, and `np-crossns-dev`, which carries no labels of its own.

Create a NetworkPolicy named `payments-ingress` in the `np-crossns` namespace that allows traffic to `payments` on TCP port `80` from Pods running in any namespace labelled `purpose=monitoring`, and from nowhere else.

Do not modify the `default-deny` policy, and do not add or remove any namespace label.

verification.description: payments-ingress applies Ingress rules to the app=payments Pods
The probe Pod in the monitoring namespace can reach payments
The probe Pod in the unlabelled namespace is denied

questions.question:
The `np-combined` namespace runs the Pod `ledger` (label `app=ledger`, serving HTTP on port `80`) and already carries a NetworkPolicy named `default-deny` that denies all ingress.

Three Pods elsewhere may try to reach it:

- `collector` (label `app=collector`) in `np-combined-platform`, a namespace labelled `tier=platform`
- `auditor` (label `app=auditor`) in `np-combined-platform`
- `collector` (label `app=collector`) in `np-combined-edge`, a namespace with no labels of its own

Create a NetworkPolicy named `ledger-ingress` in the `np-combined` namespace that allows traffic to `ledger` on TCP port `80` only from Pods that are labelled `app=collector` **and** are running in a namespace labelled `tier=platform`.

Of the three Pods listed above, only the first may reach `ledger`.

Do not modify the `default-deny` policy, and do not change any Pod or namespace label.

verification.description: The collector Pod in the platform namespace can reach ledger
The auditor Pod in the platform namespace is denied
The collector Pod in the unlabelled namespace is denied

questions.question:
The `np-egress` namespace runs three Pods: `orders` (label `app=orders`), `catalog` (label `app=catalog`, serving HTTP on port `80`) and `reports` (label `app=reports`, serving HTTP on port `80`). The Services `catalog` and `reports` point at the last two.

Create a NetworkPolicy named `orders-egress` in the `np-egress` namespace that restricts outgoing traffic from the Pods labelled `app=orders` so that they may reach only:

- the Pods labelled `app=catalog`, on TCP port `80`
- cluster DNS, which runs in the `kube-system` namespace and answers on port `53` over both `UDP` and `TCP`

The policy must restrict `Egress` only, and must not contain a rule that permits all outgoing traffic.

When you are finished `orders` must be able to resolve `catalog.np-egress.svc.cluster.local` and reach `catalog` by that name, and must not be able to reach `reports`.

Do not change any Pod or Service.

verification.description: orders-egress restricts egress and allows DNS over UDP and TCP
Pod orders resolves catalog.np-egress.svc.cluster.local
Pod orders reaches catalog by name on port 80
Pod orders is denied egress to reports

questions.question:
The `np-external` namespace runs the Pod `gateway` (label `app=gateway`). It calls a third-party payment provider over HTTPS on the public internet.

Cluster policy requires that the gateway may open outbound connections to any address on the internet on TCP port `443`, but must never be able to reach:

- the cluster Pod network, `10.42.0.0/16`
- the cloud instance metadata endpoint, `169.254.169.254/32`

Create a NetworkPolicy named `gateway-egress` in the `np-external` namespace that enforces exactly that.

The policy must apply to the Pods labelled `app=gateway`, must restrict `Egress` only, and must express the whole requirement in a single egress rule with a single peer and a single port. No rule in the policy may re-open a path to either excluded range.

Do not change the `gateway` Pod.

verification.description: gateway-egress applies Egress rules to the app=gateway Pods
One rule allows TCP 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 while excluding both ranges
No rule re-opens a path to the excluded ranges

questions.question:
The `np-additive` namespace runs the Pod `reports` (label `app=reports`, serving HTTP on port `80`) and two clients: `frontend` (label `role=frontend`) and `backup` (label `role=backup`).

A NetworkPolicy named `allow-frontend` already exists. It belongs to the application team, is under their change control, and must be left exactly as it is.

The backup team now needs `backup` to reach `reports` on TCP port `80` as well.

Create a NetworkPolicy named `allow-backup` in the `np-additive` namespace that grants that access.

When you are finished both `frontend` and `backup` must be able to reach `reports` on port `80`, and `allow-frontend` must still be exactly the policy it is now.

Do not modify or delete `allow-frontend`, and do not change any Pod label.

verification.description: allow-frontend is unchanged
allow-backup adds a second set of Ingress rules for app=reports
Pod backup can reach reports on port 80
Pod frontend still reaches reports on port 80

questions.question:
The `np-ports` namespace runs the Pod `payments` (label `app=payments`). It serves the application on TCP port `80` and a metrics endpoint on TCP port `9090`. Three clients share the namespace: `frontend` (label `role=frontend`), `prometheus` (label `role=monitoring`) and `batch` (label `role=batch`).

Create a NetworkPolicy named `payments-ingress` in the `np-ports` namespace that applies to the Pods labelled `app=payments` and allows:

- TCP port `80` from Pods whose `role` label is either `frontend` or `monitoring`
- TCP port `9090` from Pods labelled `role=monitoring`

The two-value client set on port `80` must be written as a single `matchExpressions` rule using the `In` operator over the `role` key, listing exactly those two values, rather than as two separate peers.

When you are finished `frontend` must reach port `80` but not `9090`, `prometheus` must reach `9090`, and `batch` must reach neither.

Do not change any Pod label.

verification.description: payments-ingress uses a matchExpressions In rule and a separate 9090 rule
Pod frontend can reach payments on port 80
Pod frontend is denied port 9090
Pod prometheus can reach payments on port 9090
Pod batch is denied both ports

questions.question:
The `checkout` Deployment in the `np-ts-selector-clients` namespace can no longer reach the `inventory` Pod in the `np-ts-selector` namespace. Every request times out.

`inventory` (label `app=inventory`) serves HTTP on port `80` and sits behind the `inventory` Service. A NetworkPolicy named `inventory-ingress` was written to permit exactly the `checkout` Pods and nothing else, and it is still in place.

The `np-ts-selector-clients` namespace is labelled `access=inventory` and also runs an unrelated Pod named `scanner` (label `app=scanner`), which must never be able to reach `inventory`.

Investigate and restore the intended access.

When you are finished the `checkout` Pods must be able to reach `inventory` on port `80`, `scanner` must not, the `checkout` Deployment must still declare `2` replicas, and `inventory-ingress` must still exist and still apply to the Pods labelled `app=inventory`.

Do not change any Pod or namespace label.

verification.description: inventory-ingress and the checkout Deployment are intact
A checkout Pod can reach inventory on port 80
Pod scanner remains denied while checkout works

questions.question:
A NetworkPolicy named `vault-isolation` was added to the `np-ts-inert` namespace to lock down the `vault` Pod, but nothing changed: every Pod in the namespace can still reach it.

`vault` (label `app=vault`) serves HTTP on port `80` and sits behind the `vault` Service. The namespace also runs `auditor` (label `role=auditor`), which is authorised to reach `vault` on port `80`, and `intruder` (label `role=intruder`), which is not.

Investigate and make the policy do what it was written to do.

When you are finished `auditor` must still be able to reach `vault` on port `80`, `intruder` must not, and `vault-isolation` must still exist.

Do not delete the policy, and do not change the labels of any Pod — the `vault` Service selects its Pod by label.

verification.description: vault-isolation now selects the vault Pod, whose labels are unchanged
Pod auditor keeps its access to vault
Pod intruder is denied access to vault

questions.question:
The Pod `sync-agent` in the `np-ts-egress` namespace cannot reach the `archive` Service in the `np-ts-egress-store` namespace. Every request fails.

`archive` (label `app=archive`) serves HTTP on port `80` and already carries a NetworkPolicy named `archive-ingress` that admits the `np-ts-egress` namespace on that port. That policy and the `archive` workload belong to the storage team and must not be touched.

A third namespace, `np-ts-egress-decoy`, runs a Pod named `secrets-api` that `sync-agent` must never be able to reach.

Investigate and restore the intended access.

When you are finished `sync-agent` must be able to reach `archive.np-ts-egress-store.svc.cluster.local` on port `80`, and must still be unable to reach anything in `np-ts-egress-decoy`.

Do not modify or delete `archive-ingress`, and do not change the `archive` Pod.

verification.description: sync-agent reaches archive by its fully qualified name
archive-ingress and the archive workload are unchanged
sync-agent still cannot reach the decoy namespace

questions.question:
The `np-design` namespace runs a three-tier application as three Pods: `web` (label `tier=web`, serving port `80`), `api` (label `tier=api`, serving port `8080`) and `db` (label `tier=db`, serving port `5432`). Each sits behind a Service of the same name. The `np-design-clients` namespace, labelled `role=edge`, runs `ingress-gw` (label `role=gateway`) and `rogue` (label `role=rogue`).

The `np-design` namespace currently has no NetworkPolicy at all. Design and apply whatever policies are needed there so that exactly the following holds:

- `ingress-gw` may reach the web tier on TCP `80`
- the web tier may reach the api tier on TCP `8080`
- the api tier may reach the db tier on TCP `5432`
- the web tier may not reach the db tier
- `ingress-gw` may not reach the api tier or the db tier
- `rogue` may reach nothing in `np-design`
- every tier may resolve names through cluster DNS

Both directions must be restricted: each tier's outgoing traffic must be limited to what the list above allows, and the tiers address each other by Service name.

No policy you create may contain a rule that permits all traffic, and none may name `0.0.0.0/0`.

You may create as many policies as you like, with names of your choosing. Do not change any Pod, Service, or label.

verification.description: ingress-gw can reach the web tier on port 80
The web tier can reach the api tier by name on port 8080
The api tier can reach the db tier by name on port 5432
The web tier is denied direct access to the db tier
ingress-gw is denied access to the api tier
Pod rogue is denied access to the web tier
No policy in np-design contains a blanket allow rule
